newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican anti-drug cops resent growing army role.
newsitem.headline: Mexican anti-drug cops resent growing army role.

text.p: Mexican anti-drug agents on Tuesday staged a demonstration at the attorney general's office protesting the growing role of the military in the country's anti-narcotics efforts.
More than 100 so-called "Federales", many wearing their trademark sunglasses and black leather jackets, sought an audience with attorney general Jorge Medrazo Cuellar, to present a list of concerns.
"The problem is that the Federal Judicial Police has tried to put in non-police," Commander Victor Blancas, the only member of the protesters prepared to identify himself, said.

Military officers have recently replaced career policemen from the highest ranks on down in a move aimed at rooting out corruption that has been criticised by leftist politicians as a sign of the growing militarization of Mexico.
This week some 3,000 soldiers took on police work in the capital while their civilian counterparts were sent on two-month military training courses.
The attorney general did not meet the protesters, but they were received by a lower-ranking official who agreed to pass on their message to Madrazo.
